x: Clive Ryan's time, recorded twice this year, equals Frank Kemp's record set up in July, 1950.

Could it be that the activities of Ibbotson & Co. have frightened them into premature retirement? In the junior match Clive Ryan accomplished a very good double by winning both the 220 & 440 yds, the latter in 51.1s.

Although entries were only average in number a very fine Championship meeting was held and some really excellent performances were witnessed. Outstanding amongst these were the doubles of Clive Ryan in the 100 and 220 yds. and John Davies in the 880yds and 1 mile.

Our own John Davies, Brian Morris, Clive Ryan, Frank Wright and D. McCorquindale were competing elsewhere, and with Stan Vickers Eric Hall, Norman Caves, Mal Ash and Andorka also unavailable our team could not be said to be truly representative of the name of Belgrave.
On Saturday Clive Ryan and Charlie Jones comfortably qualified for the 440 final despite being drawn against each other in their heat and having to fill first two places.
Most notable of these were the 440 yds. win in 48·7s. by Clive Ryan - a new Championship record, and the mile win of Malcolm Robinson in which Jack Brown's long standing record only just survived.

With 50.2 Clive Ryan qualified for the final, but was unable to reproduce a similar time. With three to qualify in the 880 yards heats both John Thresher and Bob Taylor (Capt) finished fourth in their respective heats.
Last year it was Rangit Bhatia in the mile; the year previous Clive Ryan in the 440. This year Bob ran in the event sandwiched by these two - the 880 yards.

Jay Busk (1) is about to unleash the fastest one lap performance in the Championships since Clive Ryan's 48.7 for 440 yards four years before Jay was born! Guy Sagar (lane 2) took second. In lane 3 is Gareth Allison who set a Youths club record for 400mH a couple of weeks later.
